The area of $ABCD$ is $101{\text{ in}}^{2}.$ What is the area of $△BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 18\cdot 20\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{90}^{∘} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 360\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{90}^{∘} \\ & ≈180{\text{ mi}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\ & =180-105 \\ & =75{\text{ mi}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

rounded to the **nearest integer**.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 

$$
